title: Basic Accounting Procedures – Journal entries
outcomes: Explain the two-sided (double entry) effect of every transaction and why it lets you check the books.
Classify accounts as personal (natural, artificial, representative), real or nominal — and under the accounting-equation (modern) approach.
Decide the debit and the credit for any transaction using the golden rules or the accounting equation, and get the same answer both ways.
Write journal entries in the exam format — date, particulars, L.F., amounts and a narration — including compound and special entries.
Record GST on purchases, sales and expenses using input and output tax accounts, set-off and payment.

meta.exam_tip: Journal entries appear in almost every Paper 1 question — a wrong debit/credit here costs marks later in ledgers, trial balance and final accounts.

concepts.title: Double entry: every rupee has a source and a use
body: Every transaction changes at least two accounts, and the total debited always equals the total credited. Buy furniture for cash: furniture goes up, cash goes down — both are recorded.
Because both sides are always written, the books can be tested (the trial balance), profit can be worked out in detail, and the financial position can be shown at any date.
concepts.analogy: A see-saw: whatever weight you put on one side must be matched on the other, or it tips. An entry with unequal sides is a see-saw lying on the ground — something is missing.
concepts.work: Accounting software refuses to save a voucher whose debits and credits differ. When an auditor finds a difference in the books, the first question is: which entry was only half recorded?

concepts.title: An account, a debit and a credit
body: An account is a summary of all increases and decreases in one item — Cash, Rent, Rohan. It is shown in a T shape: left side = debit (Dr), right side = credit (Cr).
Debit and credit are only positions — left and right. "Credit" is not good news and "debit" is not bad news. Whether an amount goes left or right depends on the type of account.
concepts.analogy: Think of the two columns of a cricket scorecard — runs scored and runs given. Neither column is "good"; you need both to know the result.
concepts.work: A client says "the bank credited my account". From the bank's books, your deposit is money it owes you (a liability), so the bank credits you. In your own books, the same deposit is a debit to Bank A/c. Explaining this perspective is daily work for a CA.

concepts.title: The accounting equation (modern approach)
body: Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Every transaction keeps this equation true.
Rules: an increase in an asset, an expense or drawings is debited; an increase in a liability, capital or income is credited. Decreases go the opposite way.

head: Transaction
Assets (₹)
Liabilities (₹)
Capital (₹)
blocks.note: Furniture for cash only swaps one asset for another (cash down, furniture up), so the totals do not move. Sale: stock ₹20,000 goes out, cash ₹25,000 comes in — net assets +₹5,000, and the ₹5,000 profit raises capital.

concepts.analogy: Your business is a bag. What is inside the bag (assets) must always equal what the bag owes to outsiders (liabilities) plus what it owes to the owner (capital).
concepts.work: Analysts read a balance sheet using exactly this equation. A sudden jump in assets with no rise in liabilities or capital is a red flag that an entry is wrong.

concepts.title: Traditional classification and the three golden rules
body: Personal accounts — people and bodies: natural persons (Rohan), artificial or legal persons (a company, a bank, a club) and representative personal accounts that stand for a person (Outstanding Salary, Prepaid Rent, Capital, Drawings). Rule: debit the receiver, credit the giver.
Real accounts — things owned: tangible (cash, machinery, stock) and intangible (goodwill, patents, trademarks). Rule: debit what comes in, credit what goes out.
Nominal accounts — expenses, losses, incomes, gains (rent, salary, commission received, discount allowed). Rule: debit all expenses and losses, credit all incomes and gains.
concepts.analogy: Personal = who? Real = what? Nominal = why? Ask the three questions and the account type usually becomes obvious.
concepts.work: When you create ledgers in accounting software you choose a group (Sundry Debtors, Fixed Assets, Indirect Expenses). Picking the wrong group misplaces the item in the financial statements — the same thinking as classifying accounts.

concepts.title: The journal: book of original entry
body: Each entry shows: date; the account debited (with "Dr.") and, on the next line, the account credited (starting with "To"); ledger folio (L.F.); debit and credit amounts; and a short narration in brackets beginning "Being …".
A compound entry has more than one debit or credit (for example, a payment with discount). An opening entry brings last year's balances into the new books.

Special cases: trade discount is never recorded (record the net price); cash discount is recorded (Discount Allowed/Received). Goods taken for personal use: Drawings Dr, To Purchases. Free samples: Advertisement Dr, To Purchases. Goods lost by fire: Loss by Fire Dr (and Insurance Claim Dr for the admitted claim), To Purchases.
concepts.analogy: The journal is a diary in date order; the ledger is the same information sorted into folders, one folder per account.
concepts.work: Every journal entry must be supported by a document — invoice, receipt, debit note, bank statement. "Vouching" (checking entries against documents) is one of the first audit tasks an articled assistant does.

concepts.title: Accounting for GST
body: GST paid on purchases and expenses is debited to Input CGST/SGST (supply within the same State) or Input IGST (supply between States). It is not part of the cost when the credit is available — it is an amount recoverable from the government.
GST collected on sales is credited to Output CGST/SGST or Output IGST — a liability payable to the government.
At the end of the period, input tax is set off against output tax (Output … A/c Dr, To Input … A/c) and only the balance is paid. Credit of CGST cannot be used to pay SGST and vice versa.
concepts.analogy: GST is like a parcel you carry for the government: you collect it from customers, subtract what you already paid to suppliers, and hand over only the difference.
concepts.work: Every month accountants match input tax in the books with what suppliers have reported, pass the set-off entry and pay the net tax. Errors here lead to interest and notices — a common reason clients call their CA.

jobs.title: Vouching purchase entries in your first audit
jobs.role: Articled assistant at a CA firm (statutory audit of a wholesaler)
jobs.situation: Your senior asks you to vouch 25 purchase entries for March. Three things turn up: one entry records the list price and shows the trade discount as "Discount Received"; one supplier invoice has no matching entry; and the proprietor's personal phone bill is booked as Telephone Expenses.
steps: Pick the sample from the purchase register and pull each supplier invoice.
Match date, supplier, net amount and GST with the entry. Trade discount should simply reduce the amount — it is not income.
Search later entries and the supplier's statement for the missing invoice; if it is truly missing, it is an unrecorded liability.
The personal phone bill should be Drawings, not an expense — it overstates expenses and understates the proprietor's withdrawals.
Write each finding in the working paper with the document reference and the correct entry, and discuss with your senior.
jobs.takeaway: Journal rules are not just exam rules — auditors test every entry against them. A misclassification changes profit, capital or liabilities.
jobs.think: Why does recording trade discount as income overstate both purchases and income, even though profit stays the same?
jobs.answer: Purchases are recorded at the list price (too high) and an equal amount appears as discount income, so both totals are inflated by the same figure and the net effect on profit is nil — but the accounts are misleading.

jobs.title: Month-end GST entries for a small business
jobs.role: Accounts executive in a trading company
jobs.situation: It is the 5th of the month. Your manager wants the GST payable for last month and the entries posted before the return is filed.
steps: Total the Output CGST, SGST and IGST ledgers from the sales side.
Total the Input tax ledgers and reconcile them with what suppliers have reported, so that credit is taken only where it is available.
Pass the set-off entries: Output … A/c Dr, To Input … A/c — never using CGST credit against SGST or the other way round.
Pass the payment entry for the balance and keep the challan as the supporting document.
jobs.takeaway: Input tax is an asset until it is set off; output tax is a liability until it is paid. Your ledgers should tell you the GST position on any day.
jobs.think: Output CGST ₹48,000, Input CGST ₹52,000. What is the CGST payable in cash this month?
jobs.answer: Nil. Input credit exceeds output tax, so the extra ₹4,000 remains as Input CGST (an asset) to be used later.

mcqs.q: Goods costing ₹6,000 were taken by the proprietor for personal use. The correct entry is:
options: Drawings A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c
Purchases A/c Dr. To Drawings A/c
Drawings A/c Dr. To Sales A/c
Capital A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
mcqs.explain: The proprietor receives the goods, so Drawings (representing the owner's withdrawal) is debited; the goods leave the business at cost, so Purchases is credited, reducing the goods available for sale. The tempting option credits Sales, but no sale has taken place — there is no customer and no revenue, so cost, not selling price, is used. In practice: when a kirana shop owner takes groceries home, the accountant records ₹6,000 as drawings against purchases at cost.

mcqs.q: Goods with a list price of ₹50,000 are bought at 10% trade discount and 2% cash discount for immediate payment. The cash paid is:
mcqs.explain: Trade discount is deducted first: ₹50,000 × 90% = ₹45,000, the invoice amount. Cash discount is then given on this amount: 2% of ₹45,000 = ₹900, so cash paid = ₹45,000 − ₹900 = ₹44,100. The tempting ₹44,000 deducts 12% straight from the list price, wrongly applying both discounts to ₹50,000. In practice: suppliers offer terms such as '2/7, net 30' to encourage early payment, and the cash discount is booked as discount received.

Prepaid insurance means the insurer has received money for cover not yet given, so the insurer effectively owes the business. Such accounts, which represent persons, are representative personal accounts. The tempting option, a nominal account, would apply to Insurance (expense) Account; once the premium relates to a future period, it represents a person who owes the business. In practice: prepaid insurance appears under other current assets in the year-end balance sheet.

mcqs.q: Under the accounting-equation approach, an increase in a liability is:
mcqs.explain: Under the accounting equation approach, increases in assets and expenses are debited, while increases in liabilities, capital and incomes are credited. An increase in a liability is therefore credited. The tempting option, 'debited', applies when a liability decreases, for example on paying a creditor. In practice: when a business buys goods on credit from a supplier, the supplier's account (a liability) is credited, increasing the amount owed.

Real accounts record things the business owns. Goodwill is owned and has value, but cannot be touched or seen, so it is an intangible real account; patents and trademarks are similar. The tempting option, nominal account, is for expenses, losses, incomes and gains — goodwill is an asset carried forward, not an expense of the period. In practice: goodwill appears in Indian balance sheets when a business buys another and pays more than the fair value of its net assets.

mcqs.q: Output CGST ₹12,500, Output SGST ₹12,500, Input CGST ₹9,000, Input SGST ₹9,000. Total GST to be paid in cash is:
mcqs.explain: Input tax credit is set off against output tax head by head. CGST payable = ₹12,500 − ₹9,000 = ₹3,500; SGST payable = ₹12,500 − ₹9,000 = ₹3,500; total paid in cash = ₹7,000. The tempting ₹3,500 counts only one head, forgetting that CGST and SGST are separate taxes paid separately. In practice: registered businesses file GSTR-3B monthly, set off input credit in the electronic credit ledger and pay the balance through the electronic cash ledger.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a nominal account?
mcqs.explain: Nominal accounts record expenses, losses, incomes and gains. Discount received is a gain to the business, so it is a nominal account, closed to profit and loss at year end. The tempting option, outstanding rent, sounds like an expense, but it represents the landlord to whom rent is owed — a representative personal account. Bank overdraft is personal and machinery is real. In practice: discount received appears under other income in the profit and loss account.

mcqs.q: An entry that debits two accounts and credits one is called:
mcqs.explain: A compound journal entry has more than one debit or more than one credit, or both, so an entry debiting two accounts and crediting one is compound. The tempting option, a contra entry, is a cash book term for a transaction between cash and bank (such as depositing cash into the bank). Opening and rectifying entries describe purpose, not structure. In practice: paying salaries and rent together by one cheque is recorded as a compound entry debiting both expenses and crediting bank.

mcqs.q: Capital is ₹3,00,000 and liabilities are ₹1,20,000. Total assets must be:
mcqs.explain: The accounting equation is Assets = Liabilities + Capital, so Assets = ₹1,20,000 + ₹3,00,000 = ₹4,20,000. The tempting ₹1,80,000 subtracts liabilities from capital; but both liabilities and capital are claims on the assets, so they are added. In practice: every balance sheet balances because total assets equal the combined claims of outsiders (liabilities) and the owner (capital).

mcqs.q: Goods costing ₹4,000 distributed as free samples are recorded as:
options: Advertisement A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c
Purchases A/c Dr. To Advertisement A/c
Drawings A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c
mcqs.explain: Free samples are distributed to promote the business, so their cost is an advertisement (sales promotion) expense and Advertisement A/c is debited. The goods leave the business at cost, so Purchases is credited. The tempting option debits Drawings, which applies only when the owner takes goods for personal use, not when goods are given away to promote sales. In practice: pharmaceutical companies record doctors' samples as sales promotion expenses at cost, not at selling price.

summary: Every transaction has equal debit and credit effects (double entry).
Golden rules — Personal: debit the receiver, credit the giver. Real: debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Nominal: debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains.
Modern rule — assets, expenses, drawings increase by debit; liabilities, capital, incomes increase by credit.
Journal format: Date | Particulars (Dr line, then "To" line) | L.F. | Dr | Cr, with narration.
GST: input tax is debited (recoverable), output tax credited (payable); set off, then pay the balance.
remember: Trade discount — never recorded. Cash discount — always recorded.
Drawings of goods / free samples / goods lost: always credit Purchases at cost.
CGST credit cannot pay SGST and SGST credit cannot pay CGST.
traps: Don't debit Purchases when buying an asset like furniture — debit the asset account.
Don't record the list price; record the net invoice price.
Don't forget the insurance claim admitted when goods are lost.

viva.q: What is the double entry system of book-keeping?
viva.model: Under the double entry system every transaction has two aspects, so at least two accounts are affected. One account is debited and another is credited with the same amount. Because every debit has an equal credit, the total of all debits equals the total of all credits, which lets us check arithmetical accuracy through a trial balance.

viva.q: Explain input tax, output tax and set-off under GST in the books of a registered trader.
viva.model: Input tax is the GST paid on purchases; it is recoverable, so the Input CGST and Input SGST accounts are debited like an asset. Output tax is the GST charged on sales; it is payable to the government, so the Output tax accounts are credited as a liability. At the end of the period input tax is set off against output tax, and only the balance is paid. CGST credit cannot be used to pay SGST and SGST credit cannot be used to pay CGST.

cases.title: Meera Traders — first week of business
cases.case: Meera starts a stationery business on 1 August 2026 with cash of ₹2,00,000. On 2 August she buys goods from Vinay & Sons with a list price of ₹1,00,000 at a trade discount of 15%, on credit. On 6 August she pays Vinay & Sons in cash and, because she pays within the week, receives a cash discount of 2% on the amount due. On 8 August she donates goods costing ₹5,000 to a local school. No other cash transaction takes place.

mcqs.q: At what amount will the purchase of 2 August be recorded?
mcqs.explain: Trade discount is a reduction in the list price given on the invoice and is never recorded in the books. The purchase is recorded at the invoice value: ₹1,00,000 × 85% = ₹85,000. The tempting ₹1,00,000 records the list price, but that amount is never owed to the supplier. In practice: GST is also calculated on the price after trade discount, so the invoice figure is the base used throughout the books.

mcqs.q: How much cash does Meera pay Vinay & Sons on 6 August?
mcqs.explain: Cash discount is calculated on the amount actually due after trade discount: ₹85,000 × 98% = ₹83,300 paid. The discount of ₹1,700 (2% of ₹85,000) is credited to Discount Received as a gain. The tempting ₹83,000 deducts 2% of the list price (₹2,000) instead of 2% of the amount due. In practice: suppliers in wholesale trade often allow such prompt-payment discounts to speed up cash collection.

mcqs.q: Which entry records the donation of 8 August?
options: Charity A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c
Purchases A/c Dr. To Charity A/c
Drawings A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c
Charity A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
mcqs.explain: Goods donated to a school are an expense of the business, recorded as charity. The goods leave at cost, so Purchases is credited: Charity A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c ₹5,000. The tempting option debits Drawings, which would apply only if Meera took the goods for her own use. The entry crediting Cash is wrong because no cash was paid. In practice: under GST, input tax credit on goods given away free is generally blocked, so it is reversed.

mcqs.q: What is the cash balance after 8 August?
mcqs.explain: The only cash movements are capital introduced of ₹2,00,000 and the payment of ₹83,300 to Vinay & Sons, so the cash balance is ₹2,00,000 − ₹83,300 = ₹1,16,700. The tempting ₹1,15,000 assumes ₹85,000 was paid, ignoring the cash discount. The donation of goods does not affect cash at all. In practice: a cash book is prepared from actual receipts and payments only, so non-cash entries such as the donation never appear in it.
